newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car scheme seen reducing Fiat layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Italy car scheme seen reducing Fiat layoffs.

text.p: The Italian government's incentive plan to boost car sales should have positive effects on the domestic market and sharply reduce Fiat Auto's need to trim production by temporary layoffs, a trade union source said.
The source said Fiat would likely only use layoffs for February on the Alfa 155 production line at its Pomigliano plant.
Fiat is due to meet trade unions on Wednesday to officially announce its production and layoff plans for next month.

Fiat will trim production by 10,300 vehicles in the January 7 to February 2 period under plans announced in December. The carmaker has for years resorted to temporary layoffs, usually on a month by month basis, in order to align output to the stagnant state of the domestic car market.

The carmaker, which has a dominant position in Italy's market, is expected to benefit from new government measures to give bonuses to motorists who trade in cars over 10-years old for scrapping and buy new models.
